model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; cash earnings after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E net operating income (net interest income + non-interest income, ex Notable Items). FY2026 ends 30 Sep 2026 and is unreported; only a short 1H26 interim ANNOUNCEMENT was extracted (no full financial statements), so FY0 is built forward from FY2025 (22,384, WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:637-area CSV revenue) at +3.2%, roughly half of system credit growth guidance (5.7% 2025, 6.3% 2026) net of ongoing core-NIM compression (core NIM 1.81%, -1bp FY25). Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027 exactly one year from the valuation date, matching the engine's end-of-year discounting (as NAB.AX 2026-09-24).
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,420,353,305 ordinary shares fully paid at 30 Sep 2025 (WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:93, :5660), consistent with the FY2025 weighted average of 3,427m (:1867). Held FLAT: the 1H26 Dividend Reinvestment Plan is explicitly satisfied by a THIRD PARTY PURCHASING SHARES ON-MARKET, not new issuance (WBC.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:191-193: 'Westpac intends to arrange for the purchase of Westpac shares on market... to satisfy participant's DRP entitlements') -- unlike NAB's underwritten, dilutive 1H26 DRP, so no share-count adjustment is needed here. The on-market buyback (extended to Nov-2026, ~$672m FY25, ~2.5% of shares retired since 2023) roughly offsets new issuance from equity-based compensation, which is separately expensed in the flows.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt held at ZERO by construction. Westpac is an APRA-regulated ADI: customer deposits ($770.5bn FY2025, kpis CustomerDeposits) and wholesale debt issuance/loan capital ($39,970m loan capital + debt issues, core_metrics) are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; liquid assets held against that funding are not surplus cash. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (cash earnings less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = cash earnings ex-Notable Items ~7,120 less capital retained ~2,290 (= NPAT margin x g/ROTE, g=3.2%, ROTE=10.8%). Cross-check: FY2025 NPAT ex-Notables 6,972 less ordinary dividends paid (FY25 DividendsPaid 5,215, core_metrics) less buyback 672 = ~1,085 net distributed above earnings, consistent with tangible book per share falling from $18.22 (Sep-25, computed: equity 72,766 - intangibles 10,465 = 62,301 / 3,420) to $17.73 (31-Mar-26, WBC.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:169) even before the FY26 interim dividend is paid -- i.e. FY25-26 distributions are running ahead of organic FCFE, the same pattern flagged on NAB. reported_fcf = FCFE + equity-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 +9,489; FY2024 -19,767; FY2023 -10,796, metrics_normalized) is deposit/loan/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment arrangements $95m FY2025, $97m FY2024 (WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:665, :683 -- statement of changes in equity components across the halves). No separate net-share-settlement tax line disclosed. ~0.4% of net operating income, a narrow house/street band.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income ($53.9bn gross FY2025, WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:788) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 on-market buyback $672m (WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:696), down from $1,812m FY2024 and $3,503m FY2022 (core_metrics ShareRepurchases). Programme extended through Nov-2026. The flat share count is a modelling convention: the buyback funds retirement of shares issued for equity-based compensation and DRP-adjacent dilution is nil this cycle because the 1H26 DRP is satisfied by third-party on-market purchase, not new issuance.
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-09-30 (30 Sep 2025 count of 3,420.35m; no new issuance expected from the 1H26 DRP, which is satisfied on-market)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Equity attributable to owners $72,766m at 30 Sep 2025 (WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:637); total intangible assets $10,465m (:5250) -> tangible equity ~$62.3bn, NTA/share ~$18.22. At 31 Mar 2026, NTA/share $17.73 (WBC.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:169), implying tangible equity ~$60.6bn -- book fell over the half as distributions ran ahead of retained cash earnings. ROTE ex-Notable Items: 10.97% FY2025, 11.21% FY2024, 11.67% FY2023, 10.58% FY2022 (WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:10022-10023) -- a declining trend as UNITE investment ramps and cost-to-income rose from 50.7% (FY24) to 53.2%/53.0% ex-Notables (FY25, :7660-7661). CET1 ratio 12.4% at 31 Mar 2026 vs an above-11.25% target, ~$2.7bn of surplus capital (WBC.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:127-129).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in AUD, the currency of the flows: AUD 10-year Commonwealth bond ~4.3% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.0 x Australian equity risk premium 5.4% = 9.7%, the same rate used for NAB.AX (2026-09-24) for cross-bank comparability -- Westpac is a domestic big-four peer with a similar funding mix and no materially different systematic risk. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, UNITE execution and AML/CTF regulatory risk is charged in the bear flows and the bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial ($518m at 30 Sep 2025 vs $72.8bn equity, WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:1783); lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. Non-controlling interests are immaterial for Westpac (no separate NCI profit-share line comparable to NAB's disclosed in the extracted filings); the modelled 31.0% cash-tax rate (effective tax rate 30.97% FY2025, :1744) absorbs any minor NCI leakage. No separate NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (same approach as NAB.AX 2026-09-24, MQG.AX and IAG.AX 2026-09-23; SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book, and FCFE with retention = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE) is the clean-surplus equivalent, run through the validated slider engine which also produces the workbook). Engine mapping: revenue = net operating income ex-Notable Items; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax cash margin (100 - cost-to-income ratio - credit impairment charge as % of NOI) PLUS equity-based compensation as % of NOI (FY2025 45.5%: 100 - 53.0 - 1.9 + 0.4, cross-checked against NPAT ex-Notables 6,972 / FY2025 revenue 22,384 via a 31% tax rate: implied NPAT ~7,032 vs actual 6,972, ~1% variance from rounding/minor NCI); sbc_pct_path = 0.4%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation/software amortisation sits inside operating expenses, a genuine cost for a bank, not an add-back); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the CET1 target = NPAT margin x g/ROTE; cash_tax_rate_path = 31.0% (FY2025 effective rate 30.97%); wacc = cost of equity 9.7%; net_debt = 0. LARGE-ITEM CAVEAT: unlike NAB, no comparable large 1H26 notable item was found in the (thin) extracted 1H26 filing -- the FY0 build instead steps forward from the FY2025 annual, which is the most recent full financial statement available. H2 FY2026 (Apr-Sep 2026) is unreported and the 1H26 filing extracted here is a short results-announcement/investor summary, not the full interim financial report, so 1H26 detail (segment P&L, full balance sheet, weighted-average shares) is thinner than ideal -- refresh this driver set when the FY2026 annual (due ~Nov 2026) is extracted. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (10.8 - 2.5)/(9.7 - 2.5) = 1.153x x $18.22 = ~$21.0/share; the market price implies roughly 1.89x FY2025 TBV ($18.22), which requires either a sustained ROTE well above the 10.5-11% band Westpac has run since FY2022, or a cost of equity well below 9.7%. Price is the ASX regular close, not volatile (see current_price / price_as_of).

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is cash/underlying NPAT ex-Notable Items (already after equity-based compensation): FY2021 6,953; FY2022 6,568; FY2023 7,368; FY2024 7,113; FY2025 6,972 (WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:10022). The series is roughly FLAT over 4-5 years -- FY2023 was a NIM-cycle peak (core NIM benefited most from the RBA hiking cycle) and FY2024-25 show the cost-to-income drag from UNITE investment eroding what NIM and volume growth delivered. Revenue = statutory net operating income (CSV): FY2016 20,985, FY2020 20,183 (COVID), FY2022 19,606 (trough on margin compression), FY2025 22,384.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average net operating income growth (3.2% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), anchored near the 9-year revenue CAGR (0.7%) plus a credit-growth-driven near-term uplift (system housing credit guided 6.3% for 2026, business credit ~7.2%), tempered by structural core-NIM compression (-1bp FY25) and Westpac's below-system FY25 mortgage growth (0.84x system).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (1.4%) and cash-earnings CAGR (~0-2% over 3-4 years) both diverge sharply from the EPS 5-year CAGR (25.6%), but the EPS figure is measured from the FY2020 COVID provisioning trough (EPS $0.637) and is not a trend -- it mirrors the same distortion flagged on NAB.AX. Equity is held roughly flat by design: FY2021-25 dividends (118-153cps) plus buybacks (up to $3.5bn in FY2022) have distributed close to 100% of cash earnings, so equity CAGR does not describe underlying earnings power either. Growth is taken from the net operating income and cash-earnings series, not equity or EPS.

base.growth_rationale: Net operating income. FY27 3.2%: system credit growth guided at 6.3% (housing) / 7.2% (business) for 2026, but Westpac has run BELOW system in mortgages (0.84x FY25, though 1.2x in 1H26) and core NIM is flat-to-down (-1bp FY25) on broker/non-bank competition; volume growth of ~5-6% net of ~2-2.5pp of margin drift. Tapers to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP growth less structural margin compression), close to the 9-year 0.7% revenue CAGR plus a normalisation premium since FY16-25 spans two NIM cycles.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax cash margin (100 - cost-to-income - credit impairment charge as % of NOI) + SBC. FY26E 45.4%: CTI 53.0% (UNITE ramp continues per FY26 guided $850-950m investment, re-planned after the single-deposit-ledger decision pushed full benefits to FY28/29) and CIC still low at ~2% of NOI (~5bp of loans, near the FY2025 historic low) but drifting up from 1H26's new energy-sector overlay. FY27-28: CIC keeps normalising toward 4% of NOI as the credit cycle turns modestly, while CTI is still elevated (51.5-52.5%) before UNITE's first benefits land -- hence the mild dip to 44.9%. FY29 onward: CTI falls toward 47.0% as UNITE substantially delivers (still above CBA/NAB-level efficiency, reflecting Westpac's legacy multi-platform disadvantage flagged in Analysis.json) and CIC stabilises near 6% of NOI (~15bp of loans, a plausible mid-cycle level vs FY19's 794m/~9bp). Terminal margin 47.4% is below NAB's 47.2% mature CTI-adjusted margin plus SBC, reflecting Westpac's persistent cost-to-income disadvantage versus peers.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 above the 11.25% target as RWA grows with income = NPAT margin (~31-33% of NOI) x g / ROTE. ROTE assumed to recover mildly from FY2025's 10.97% (which itself was below FY2023's 11.67% peak) to ~11.5% by the terminal year as UNITE costs abate, i.e. 10.8% -> 11.5% across the path. At 3.2% growth ~9.3% of NOI is retained (~70% distributed, close to WBC's actual FY25 payout of 75.6% ex-Notables); at 2.5% terminal growth ~7.1% retained (~78% distributed). Cross-check: FY2025 actual retention (NPAT ex-Notables 6,972 less dividends 5,215 less buyback 672 = ~1,085) implies WBC distributed MORE than the model's steady-state retention that year, consistent with the observed fall in NTA/share into 1H26.

bull.growth_rationale: Mortgage momentum builds past system (1.2x in 1H26 sustained and improved further), business/institutional lending keeps compounding at teens growth (16-17% YoY in 1H26), NZ recovers faster than expected, and core NIM stabilises rather than eroding further as deposit and hedge dynamics turn favourable. NOI grows 4.5-5.0% near term fading to 3.0% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: UNITE delivers ahead of the re-planned schedule (single deposit ledger migration completes early, full benefits by FY27-28 rather than FY29), taking CTI from 52.0% toward ~43.0% by the terminal year -- a bigger step-change than NAB's bull case, reflecting how much more of Westpac's cost base is currently locked in legacy multi-platform overhead. Credit stays benign at 4.0% of NOI (~10bp), below the FY2025 actual normalisation path, as the AUSTRAC/CORE remediation overhang (fully resolved Oct-2025) frees management bandwidth and no new large conduct issue emerges.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin (32-37% of NOI) x g / ROTE, with ROTE lifting from 11.5% to 14.0% as cost-out and volume growth both improve returns. Higher growth still needs more capital even at a better return; terminal 3.0% growth retains ~21% of NPAT (~79% distributed).

bear.growth_rationale: The rate-cycle reversal Westpac's own economists flagged in September 2026 (RBA hikes to 4.6% by November 2026) hits mortgage serviceability just as consumer sentiment fell 5.2% in the same month; housing and business credit stress emerges through FY27-28 (mirroring the FY2020 COVID-provisioning shock in magnitude if not cause), NZ stays weak, and broker-driven mortgage competition keeps compressing the front book even as funding costs rise. NOI stalls at 0-1.5% growth.
bear.margin_rationale: CIC spikes to 8-12% of NOI in FY27-28 (comparable in relative terms to FY2020's 3,178m/~16% of that year's revenue) as the credit cycle turns; CTI simultaneously worsens to 54.5-56% as UNITE is re-planned yet again amid AML/CTF reform costs (effective 31 Mar 2026) and any fresh conduct/regulatory matter consumes management bandwidth exactly when cost discipline is most needed. Recovers only partially to a 42.9% terminal margin (CTI 51%, CIC 6.5%) -- UNITE's structural benefits never fully materialise in this case, leaving Westpac's cost-to-income disadvantage versus CBA/NAB permanently wider.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin (22-30% of NOI) x g / ROTE 6-9%; FY27 (0% growth) needs no net capital retention on the model's clean-surplus formula, but in practice RWA migration and provisioning in a downturn consumes capital regardless of book growth (the FY2020 precedent: WBC's CET1 fell and dividends were cut to 31.25cps that year) -- the model likely understates true capital consumption in this scenario, which is a conservative bias toward the DOWNSIDE case being even worse than shown.

scenario_narratives.base: Westpac grows net operating income at 3.0-3.5% fading to 2.5%, roughly matching system credit growth net of continued core-NIM compression from broker and non-bank mortgage competition. Cost-to-income stays elevated near 53% through FY27-28 as the re-planned UNITE programme (full benefits now pushed to FY28/29 after the single-deposit-ledger decision) continues to ramp, then improves toward 47% by the mid-2030s -- still worse than peers, reflecting Westpac's persistent legacy-platform cost disadvantage. Credit impairments normalise up from FY2025's historically low ~5bp of loans toward a more typical ~15bp. Cash earnings hold roughly flat near $7bn through the UNITE investment years before resuming growth, and 70-80% of them are distributed as dividends and buybacks. At a 9.7% cost of equity and a ~10.8-11.5% return on tangible equity, the franchise is worth roughly 1.15x tangible book, well below the ~1.9x the market currently pays on FY2025 tangible book of $18.22/share.
scenario_narratives.bull: UNITE delivers ahead of its re-planned schedule, taking cost-to-income from the low-50s toward the low-40s by the mid-2030s as the single-deposit-ledger migration completes cleanly and digital/AI investment cuts servicing costs faster than guided. Business, institutional and NZ lending keep compounding at high-single to low-double digits, mortgage share stabilises as the proprietary channel holds up against brokers, and credit stays benign with the AUSTRAC/CORE remediation overhang fully behind the bank. Return on tangible equity lifts from ~11% to ~14%. Even this case falls short of the current market price at a 9.7% cost of equity -- the market is pricing a cost-to-income structure and sustained ROTE Westpac has not delivered in a decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: The rate-cycle reversal Westpac's own economists flagged for late 2026 (RBA hikes back to 4.6%) collides with fixed-rate mortgage repricing and already-falling consumer sentiment, triggering a credit-impairment spike (8-12% of net operating income) reminiscent of the FY2020 COVID-provisioning year. UNITE is re-planned again as AML/CTF reform compliance costs (effective March 2026) and any fresh conduct matter consume management bandwidth, keeping cost-to-income near 54-56% for two years. Growth stalls near zero, return on tangible equity falls to high single digits, and capital retention likely needs to run ahead of the clean-surplus formula shown here as RWA migration bites in a downturn -- as it did when Westpac cut its dividend in FY2020.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%, matching NAB.AX (2026-09-24): Westpac carries the same big-four credit-cycle exposure PLUS bank-specific execution risk that is arguably worse -- UNITE has already been re-planned once (single-deposit-ledger decision pushed full benefits from FY28 to FY29), cost-to-income rose the wrong way in FY25 (50.7% to 53.2%) even before the flagged RBA rate-hike reversal, and Westpac's own economists are forecasting the tightening cycle that would trigger the bear case. Bull cut to 25%: it requires UNITE to outperform a programme that has already slipped once, sustained double-digit business-lending growth, and benign credit simultaneously, while the market at ~1.9x tangible book already prices a return on equity well above anything Westpac has delivered since FY2023.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A big-four bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at an AUD cost of equity, never on statutory operating cash flow (deposit and loan movement) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. Cash earnings ex Notable Items are the flow; capital retention to hold CET1 above target as risk-weighted assets grow is the reinvestment; 9.7% is the return an owner requires, matched to the same rate used for NAB.AX for cross-bank comparability. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a ~10.8-11.5% base-case return on tangible equity and 2.5% terminal growth, the franchise is worth roughly 1.15x tangible book (~$21/share on FY2025 tangible book of $18.22), well below the ~1.9x (current_price / $18.22 FY2025 TBV) the market currently pays. That premium requires either a sustained ROTE well above what Westpac has delivered since its FY2023 NIM-cycle peak (11.67%), or a cost of equity meaningfully below 9.7%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: FY2025's credit impairment charge (424m, ~5bp of loans) is a cyclical low; every 10bp on ~$852bn of net loans is roughly $850m pre-tax (~9% of cash earnings), and Westpac's own economists now forecast an RBA tightening reversal that would test mortgage serviceability

Net interest margin: core NIM already contracted 1bp in FY25 to 1.81% on broker/non-bank mortgage competition and deposit mix shift; 5bp on ~$1,000bn of average interest-earning assets is roughly $500m of NOI (2.2%)

UNITE execution: the programme has already been re-planned once (single-deposit-ledger decision pushed full benefits from FY28 to FY29) and cost-to-income moved the wrong way in FY25 (50.7% to 53.2%) even before that slip fully bites; a second re-plan would push the base case's margin recovery out further

Regulatory: AML/CTF reform takes effect 31 March 2026 against a bank with a A$1.3bn AUSTRAC penalty history; multi-regulator engagement (APRA, ASIC, ATO, ACCC, AUSTRAC, RBNZ and others) is a recurring cost and reputational risk noted in Analysis.json

Capital and distributions: FY2025-1H26 distributions (dividends plus buyback) have run ahead of organic FCFE, with tangible book per share falling from $18.22 (Sep-25) to $17.73 (Mar-26); a credit-cycle downturn could force either a dividend cut (as in FY2020) or slower buybacks to protect the CET1 buffer

Valuation regime: Australian bank multiples have decoupled from ROE-based models since 2023 (peers trading well above historical book-value multiples); the model is not a call on when, or whether, that regime reverts

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (ASX regular close); 52-week range 33.46-43.32.
data_sources.financials: WBC.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, AUD millions, FY2015-FY2025 annual + H1 FY2024/FY2025 halves + partial H1 FY2026) exported from WBC.AX.duckdb; kpis table for CustomerDeposits, NetInterestIncome, OperatingExpenses, CreditImpairmentCharge, CostToIncomeRatio, NetLoansAndAdvances, CashTaxesPaid, BookValuePerShare, ROE, CET1Ratio, DividendsPaid, ShareRepurchases; FY2025 Annual Report (WBC.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt) five-year performance summary (10022-10023), total equity (637), intangible assets (5250), shares on issue (93, 5660), weighted average shares (1867), effective tax rate (1744), lease liabilities (1783), share-based payments (665, 683), buyback (696), interest received/paid (788-789), CTI and Notable Items (7660-7661, 11920-11945); H1 FY2026 results announcement (WBC.AX_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) key shareholder metrics and NTA/share (169), CET1 ratio (127-129), DRP on-market-purchase mechanism (191-193) -- this is a short investor summary, not the full interim financial report, so 1H26 P&L/balance-sheet detail is thinner than the FY2025 annual.
data_sources.qualitative: WBC.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): UNITE transformation re-plan and cost-to-income trajectory, credit and NIM risks, AML/CTF reform calendar, RBA rate-hike reversal forecast by Westpac's own economists, CORE/AUSTRAC overlay removal, bull/bear cases, Sell/Neutral analyst consensus with price targets below the recent share price.
